post.summary: This action starts a genuinely self-service password reset: given only an e-mail address, with no sign-in of any kind, it looks up the matching account and -- if one exists, is not disabled, has an e-mail address on file, and this server has SMTP configured -- sends it a real reset-link e-mail via the exact same Ninlil.Web.Services.PasswordResetLinkSender round trip `UsersController.ResetPassword`'s own `EmailLink` delivery mode uses. Security-critical, deliberate departure from that admin-driven counterpart: this action's response is always the exact same Ninlil.Web.Models.ForgotPasswordResult, with the exact same `200` status, no matter which of those conditions failed -- including the "no account with this address exists at all" case. An authenticated administrator resetting a known account's password may legitimately learn whether that specific account has an e-mail address or whether SMTP is configured; a completely anonymous caller submitting an arbitrary address must never be able to use response shape, status code, or timing to enumerate which e-mail addresses have accounts on this server -- a classic account-enumeration risk for exactly this kind of endpoint. A real delivery-time failure (e.g. the SMTP server rejects the message) is caught and logged here rather than allowed to surface as a `500`, for the same reason -- an attacker distinguishing "delivery attempted and failed" from "delivery never attempted" is exactly as much of a leak as distinguishing "sent" from "not sent" would be.

This action exchanges a still-valid refresh token for a new access/refresh token pair,
revoking the refresh token it was exchanged for (rotation) so it cannot be reused. The
token comes from the request body when one is named there, otherwise from the browser's
refresh cookie -- in which case the rotated token goes back as a new cookie, not in the
body. The new session keeps the old one's Ninlil.Dns.Data.Abstractions.Entity.SessionEntity.IsPersistent
choice.

A failed cookie exchange deliberately leaves the cookie alone rather than clearing
    it. Two tabs reloading together both present the same cookie; the first rotates it,
    and the second's now-stale request fails. Had that failure cleared the cookie, its
    response would erase the fresh cookie the first tab just received and sign both
    out. Left alone, the second tab simply retries and the browser sends the rotated
    cookie. A genuinely dead cookie costs nothing but a 401; M:Ninlil.Web.Controllers.AuthController.Logout(Ninlil.Web.Models.RefreshRequest,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
    clears it.

This action revokes a refresh token, so it can no longer be exchanged for a new access
token -- the one named in the body, otherwise the browser's refresh cookie, which is
cleared either way. Possessing the raw refresh token is itself sufficient authorization
to revoke it -- the same reasoning M:Ninlil.Web.Controllers.AuthController.Refresh(Ninlil.Web.Models.RefreshRequest,System.Threading.CancellationToken) already applies -- so this
endpoint does not require a currently-valid access token.

This action completes a token-based password reset from this project's shared "set new
password" landing page -- the confirming half of both
`UsersController.ResetPassword`'s own `EmailLink` delivery mode and this
controller's own M:Ninlil.Web.Controllers.AuthController.ForgotPassword(Ninlil.Web.Models.ForgotPasswordRequest,System.Threading.CancellationToken) above, which share this exact same
confirmation action unchanged. Neither caller is authenticated at this point, so this action is
Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization.AllowAnonymousAttribute, exactly like M:Ninlil.Web.Controllers.AuthController.Login(Ninlil.Web.Models.LoginRequest,System.Threading.CancellationToken)/
M:Ninlil.Web.Controllers.AuthController.Refresh(Ninlil.Web.Models.RefreshRequest,System.Threading.CancellationToken)/M:Ninlil.Web.Controllers.AuthController.Logout(Ninlil.Web.Models.RefreshRequest,System.Threading.CancellationToken) above -- Ninlil.Web.Models.ConfirmPasswordResetRequest.Token
is the only proof of authorization this action has, checked for real by
M:Microsoft.AspNetCore.Identity.UserManager`1.ResetPasswordAsync(`0,System.String,System.String) itself (a wrong/expired/already-
consumed token fails there, not here). A missing account or an unparseable token both
report the exact same generic message, deliberately, so this action never confirms or
denies whether a given account exists.

This action creates a complete backup archive and streams it back as a downloadable

requestBody.description: The passphrase to encrypt the archive with, or omit to skip encryption.

post.summary:
This action restores this server's own full database, Data Protection key ring, TLS
certificate, and runtime configuration file from a previously created archive, of
either kind -- encrypted or, per its own envelope header, deliberately unencrypted.
Every entity currently persisted is wiped and replaced -- there is no partial or merge
restore. The archive is fully decrypted (if encrypted) and structurally validated
before any of that happens, so a rejected request (wrong or missing passphrase,
corrupted or tampered archive, unrecognized format) is guaranteed to have left this
server's own data completely untouched.

Archive.description: This property contains the backup archive to restore from, encrypted or not.

Passphrase.description:
This property contains the passphrase Ninlil.Web.Models.BackupRestoreRequest.Archive was encrypted with, if it
is an encrypted archive -- left null/blank when restoring an archive that was itself
created without one. Which case applies is detected from the archive's own contents,
not decided by whether this field is populated.

delete.summary: This action disables a single catalog entry. get.summary:
This action serves the aggregate cluster dashboard: this node's own live
query-stats snapshot, plus one row per known peer, each peer's own row collected live
over the existing TSIG-authenticated + TLS-encrypted cluster channel via
Ninlil.Dns.Server.Core.ClusterSync.IClusterQueryStatsAggregator. A peer that could not be reached is still
included in the response, marked unreachable with every count null --
never silently omitted, so an operator can tell "this peer has no query traffic" apart
from "this node could not reach this peer right now." Returns an empty peer list (this
node's own row only) when clustering is disabled or no peer is currently known.

post.summary:
This action answers a peer's own heartbeat probe. A successfully authenticated request
reaching this action at all is the entire trust decision -- this node's own
`ClusterHeartbeatBackgroundService` updates the calling peer's own
Ninlil.Dns.Data.Abstractions.Entity.ClusterNodeEntity.Status purely based on whether its own probe against
that peer succeeded, never on anything this action returns beyond a bare success
status; see that service's own doc comment for why each node's own, locally-observed
view of a peer's health is this project's deliberately chosen source of truth, not a
value the peer reports about itself.

This action receives a joining node's own callback, completing the second half of the
join handshake -- see M:Ninlil.Dns.Server.Cluster.Join.ClusterJoinService.HandleJoinCompleteAsync(System.String,Ninlil.Dns.Server.Cluster.Channel.ClusterJoinCompleteRequest,System.Threading.CancellationToken) for the
real logic this delegates to. The caller's own successfully-authenticated TSIG key name
(the exact key the invite this joiner is redeeming carried) is read from the
authenticated identity Ninlil.Dns.Server.Cluster.Authentication.ClusterTsigAuthenticationHandler already
established, never re-derived from the request body itself.

This action receives one operational-config-sync envelope from a peer and
dispatches it to whichever registered Ninlil.Dns.Server.Core.ClusterSync.IClusterConfigSyncApplier's own
Ninlil.Dns.Server.Core.ClusterSync.IClusterConfigSyncApplier.EntityType matches
Ninlil.Dns.Server.Core.ClusterSync.ClusterConfigSyncEnvelope.EntityType -- the one inbound endpoint every
synced category (filter lists, filter list entries, access-control rules, rewrites,
forwarders, settings sections) shares, per this mechanism's own "one generic envelope,
dispatched by a discriminator" design.

Always answers `200 OK`, even for an entity type this node does not recognize
    (logged, not rejected) -- a newer peer sending a category an older node has not
    been upgraded to understand yet must never look like a channel failure; the actual
    accept/reject/last-write-wins decision lives entirely inside the matched applier
    itself, per Ninlil.Dns.Server.Core.ClusterSync.IClusterConfigSyncApplier's own doc comment.

This action answers the cluster's own best-effort, cluster-wide username-uniqueness
check -- a plain, read-only existence lookup against this node's own
Ninlil.Dns.Data.Abstractions.Repository.IUserRepository, called by a peer's own
`ClusterUsernameUniquenessChecker` at user-creation time on that peer. This is
deliberately the entire check: no lock, no reservation, no two-phase commit -- a real,
if rare, race (two nodes creating the same username within the same few hundred
milliseconds, each seeing the other as not-yet-existing) is still possible, and is
exactly the case the cluster's own last-write-wins collision resolution
(Ninlil.Dns.Server.Core.ClusterSync.ClusterSyncConflictResolver, applied by
`UserClusterConfigSyncApplier`) exists to catch and flag once the two nodes'
config-sync broadcasts actually reach each other.

This action answers the aggregate cluster dashboard's per-peer query-stats
request -- a plain, read-only count against this node's own persistent query log
(Ninlil.Dns.Data.Abstractions.Repository.IDnsQueryLogRepository), called by a peer's own
`ClusterQueryStatsAggregator` when an operator opens that peer's own "Cluster"
page. Always computed live at request time, never cached -- a dashboard load tolerates
real query-log I/O far better than a DNS query answer ever could, and there is no
other consumer of this endpoint to protect from that cost.

produces, so the address is genuinely available for reallocation immediately, and any

Required; an unrecognized value is rejected by ASP.NET Core's own default model binding as an ordinary `400`, before this action's own code ever runs, the same "no hand-written validation needed for a closed, two-member choice" shape Ninlil.Web.Controllers.DhcpServiceControlController's own `{kind}` route segment already establishes. custom option it contains -- removed explicitly, rather than relying on the relational
backend's own cascade delete, since MongoDB has no equivalent mechanism at all, the same
reasoning M:Ninlil.Web.Controllers.ClientGroupsController.Delete(System.Guid,System.Threading.CancellationToken) already applies to a deleted
client group's own dependent rows. Any lease already recorded against this scope (keyed
by its own `ScopeName`, not this scope's identifier) is left untouched -- a lease is
historical/operational data, not configuration this deletion owns, the same "never
touch operational telemetry on a configuration delete" posture
`Server.Backup.BackupEntityCatalog` already establishes. A tag rule that names this
scope's own identifier (`DhcpTagRuleEntity.ScopeId`) is also left untouched -- it
simply becomes permanently ineligible to match any future client, exactly like a rule
naming a scope that was never created in the first place.

get.summary:
This action searches the query log, newest entries first, narrowed by whichever of
clientAddress/domain/queriedType/
responseCode/fromUtc/toUtc the
caller supplied.

parameters.name: clientAddress
parameters.description: An exact match against a logged entry's own client address.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: A case-insensitive substring match against a logged entry's own queried name.

parameters.name: queriedType
parameters.description:
An exact match against a logged entry's own queried record type, given by its enum
member name (for example `"A"` or `"Aaaa"`).

parameters.name: responseCode
parameters.description:
An exact match against a logged entry's own response code, given by its enum member
name (for example `"NoError"` or `"NxDomain"`).

parameters.name: fromUtc
parameters.description: The inclusive start of the time range to search.

parameters.name: toUtc
parameters.description: The inclusive end of the time range to search.

parameters.name: clientIdentifier
parameters.description: An exact match against a logged entry's own resolved, persistent client identifier (a MAC address or DUID).

parameters.name: clientProtocolVersion
parameters.description:
An exact match against a logged entry's own resolved client protocol version, given by
its enum member name (for example `"IPv4"` or `"IPv6"`) -- narrows which of
the two disjoint identifier spaces clientIdentifier must belong to.

parameters.name: Skip
parameters.description: This property contains how many items to skip before the returned page begins.

parameters.name: Take
parameters.description: This property contains the maximum number of items to return.

patch.summary:
This action merges a partial update into `DnsServer:ReverseProxy` via
Ninlil.Dns.Server.Presets.PresetConfigurationFileApplier's own generic settings-list overload, RFC
7396 merge-patch style: a field absent from patch is left exactly
as it was in the file -- including `sharedSecret`, which is always
operator-supplied (there is no server-generated value the way a TSIG key's secret can
be), so it is rotatable in place with no reveal-once problem, the same posture a cloud
provider credential's own secret already follows. `knownProxies`/
`knownNetworks` are each treated as one atomic field: present replaces the whole
array, absent leaves the stored list completely untouched -- matching
`CloudProviderCredentialsController`'s own "whole-object replacement, not a deep
merge" precedent for a field whose own shape is a collection rather than a scalar. A
`dnsOverTls` sub-object, when present, merges into the entirely separate
`DnsServer:Protocol:DnsOverTls:ProxyProtocol` section the identical way -- present
replaces the whole `knownProxies`/`knownNetworks` array, absent leaves it
untouched, mirroring `EventBrokerSettingsController`'s own `rabbitMq`/
`activeMq` nested-sub-object precedent for merging more than one configuration
section from a single `PATCH` body. There is no `sharedSecret` field inside
it at all -- see `DnsOverTlsProxyProtocolSettingsDetail`'s own doc comment for why.

get.summary: This action reads the self-update checker's own currently-known status -- whatever the most recent check (automatic or manually triggered) last recorded, never a fresh check of its own. See M:Ninlil.Web.Controllers.SelfUpdateController.Check(System.Threading.CancellationToken) to trigger a fresh one. Why there is no "apply now" button. This server has no real, safe, in-process way to replace its own running binary -- there is no installer, no systemd-unit management, and no established release-artifact packaging for this project yet (Ninlil.Dns.Server.SelfUpdate.SelfUpdateOptions's own doc comment covers the parallel gap on the feed side). Building a fake button that reports success without genuinely re-executing a new binary would be actively dishonest, and building a real one without that missing infrastructure would risk leaving a homelab DNS server half-replaced or simply dead, with nobody around to notice. Instead, Ninlil.Web.Models.SelfUpdateStatusDetail.UpdateInstructions tells an operator, in plain language, exactly what to do by hand -- an honest instruction rather than an action this project cannot yet perform safely.

get.summary: This action reports whether this host can currently answer an OIDC challenge at all, and if so, what to label the button that starts one. Deliberately checks the real, currently-registered authentication scheme, not merely Ninlil.Dns.Identity.Options.OidcSsoOptions.Enable's own raw configuration value. A write through `OidcSsoSettingsController.Patch` can flip that value without a restart, but the OpenID Connect scheme itself is only ever registered once, at process startup (see M:Ninlil.Dns.Identity.Extension.ServiceCollectionAuthenticationExtension.AddNinlilDnsAuthentication(Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.IServiceCollection,Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.IConfiguration)'s own doc comment) -- so a raw-value check here could tell the Angular login page to render a button that would 404 the moment it was clicked. Checking the scheme provider directly is the honest signal of what this specific running process can actually do right now.

This action is a real browser navigation target, not a call a single-page application
would ever `fetch()` -- it either 404s (the scheme is not registered, matching
M:Ninlil.Web.Controllers.SsoController.Get's own `enabled: false`) or issues a `302` redirect straight
to the identity provider's own authorization endpoint. There is no JSON response on
success; the eventual response the browser lands on, several redirects later, is
whatever `OnTokenValidated`/`OnRemoteFailure` sends it to (see this
controller's own doc comment).

Named M:Ninlil.Web.Controllers.SsoController.StartChallenge(System.Boolean), not `Challenge`, purely to avoid hiding
    Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.ControllerBase's own protected `Challenge(...)` helper method
    this action's own body calls -- no functional difference, just a naming collision
    to sidestep.

parameters.name: rememberMe
parameters.description:
Whether the session this sign-in ends in should outlive the browser -- the same choice
a local sign-in's "Remember me" makes. Carried through the identity provider round trip
in the challenge's own authentication properties and read back by the sign-in handler.

get.summary:

post.summary:
This action performs a real, in-process storage-engine switch: backs up this host's
currently active engine, provisions and migrates request's own
target engine, flips this process's own live storage onto it, and restores the backup
into it -- returning once every row has been carried across and this process is
already serving from the new engine. This call blocks for the whole duration of the
switch (a real backup-and-restore pass, plus a migration), which, at this project's own
stated homelab/small-org scale, is expected to complete in well under a minute.

request carries structured, per-engine connection fields (a
    file path for SQLite; host/port/database name/username/password/encryption mode for
    the other three) rather than a single free-text connection string, mirroring
    Ninlil.Web.Controllers.EventBrokerSettingsController's own structured-field pattern. This
    action assembles the real ADO.NET connection string via
    Ninlil.Web.Services.Storage.StorageConnectionStringAssembler -- always through the target
    engine's own official `*ConnectionStringBuilder` type, never by hand-formatting
    a string -- before ever calling Ninlil.Web.Services.Storage.IStorageEngineSwitchService, which
    itself still operates on that single already-assembled connection string, unaware
    structured fields exist at all.

requestBody.description: Which engine to switch to, and its own structured connection fields.

two-factor sign-in is currently required, and whether an authenticator app has already
been confirmed. Built for the self-service account-security page, which has
no other way to learn this: `UserClaimsBuilder` never places a two-factor claim on
an issued access token (a stale, cached "enabled" claim on an already-issued token
would be actively misleading the moment it changed), and the only other place this
state is exposed at all, `UsersController`'s own `UserSummary`, requires the
`users:read` permission an ordinary, non-administrative account has no reason to

post.summary:
This action generates a fresh TOTP shared secret for the current caller, replacing any
previously-generated (and not yet confirmed) one. Two-factor authentication is not yet
required at this point -- M:Ninlil.Web.Controllers.TwoFactorController.EnableAuthenticator(Ninlil.Web.Models.TwoFactorCodeRequest) must still confirm it.

This action confirms a TOTP enrollment by checking a freshly-generated code, and only
then turns on the requirement to supply a second factor at sign-in.

This action turns off the requirement to supply a second factor at sign-in, after
confirming the caller can still produce a valid code -- so a stolen access token alone
is not enough to disable this protection.

This action e-mails the current caller a one-time verification code, for use as a
second factor at sign-in when an authenticator app is not available. The caller's
e-mail address must already be confirmed.

This action generates a fresh batch of 10 single-use two-factor recovery codes for the
current caller, replacing (invalidating) any previously-generated batch entirely. Two-
factor authentication must already be enabled -- a recovery code exists purely as a
fallback for a second factor this account does not otherwise require, so generating one
first would have nothing to be a fallback *for*, mirroring the guard
M:Ninlil.Web.Controllers.TwoFactorController.EnableAuthenticator(Ninlil.Web.Models.TwoFactorCodeRequest) itself already establishes for a similar reason.

that already reports this username rejects the request outright with a

a partition; an unreachable peer is silently skipped, per this project's own explicit
"never block user management on one down peer" decision. A rarer collision that
genuinely only becomes visible after both sides already committed (a true network
partition) is instead caught and resolved later, once the two nodes resync, by
`UserClusterConfigSyncApplier`'s own last-write-wins collision handling.

from patch is left exactly as it was; a field present with a JSON
`null` clears it back to null; a field present with a string
value sets it. Ninlil.Dns.Data.Abstractions.Entity.UserEntity.Email is deliberately not accepted here -- see

post.summary:
This action changes the current caller's own password, proving they already know the
current one via M:Microsoft.AspNetCore.Identity.UserManager`1.ChangePasswordAsync(`0,System.String,System.String) -- a wrong
Ninlil.Web.Models.ChangePasswordRequest.CurrentPassword surfaces as a real, specific
Microsoft.AspNetCore.Identity.IdentityResult failure (Identity's own `PasswordMismatch` error)
through M:Ninlil.Web.Extension.IdentityResultExtension.ThrowIfFailed(Microsoft.AspNetCore.Identity.IdentityResult), never swallowed into a
generic message. See this class's own doc comment for why this needs no specific
permission, only Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization.AuthorizeAttribute.

This action resets a user account's password on an administrator's behalf -- built for
a locked-out account that cannot supply its own current password the way
M:Ninlil.Web.Controllers.UsersController.ChangeMyPassword(Ninlil.Web.Models.ChangePasswordRequest) requires. Ninlil.Web.Models.AdminResetPasswordRequest.Mode
selects one of two delivery modes (see Ninlil.Web.Models.AdminPasswordResetMode's own doc
comment for what each does and why both exist):
<list type="bullet"><item>Ninlil.Web.Models.AdminPasswordResetMode.AutoGenerate sets a freshly-generated
        strong password immediately (via a real
        M:Microsoft.AspNetCore.Identity.UserManager`1.GeneratePasswordResetTokenAsync(`0)/
        M:Microsoft.AspNetCore.Identity.UserManager`1.ResetPasswordAsync(`0,System.String,System.String) round trip, not a direct
        field write, so the exact same Identity validation/hashing path every other
        password change goes through still applies) and returns it exactly once, in
        the response body only -- this project's usual reveal-once secret exposure
        policy.
    </item><item>Ninlil.Web.Models.AdminPasswordResetMode.EmailLink e-mails the account's own
        address a link to this project's shared "set new password" landing page
        (M:Ninlil.Web.Controllers.AuthController.ResetPassword(Ninlil.Web.Models.ConfirmPasswordResetRequest) is what that page's
        own form submits to), carrying a real Identity reset token, Base64Url-encoded
        for safe transport in a URL query string -- see
        Ninlil.Web.Models.ConfirmPasswordResetRequest's own doc comment for why. Requires
        both a confirmed e-mail address on the target account and an already-configured
        SMTP server (see `SmtpSettingsController`); either gap is reported as a
        clear Ninlil.Dns.Common.Exceptions.ValidationException rather than letting
        `SmtpClient.ConnectAsync` fail with an unhelpful raw exception.
    </item></list>

both the automatic (`DnsZoneChangedEvent`-triggered) path and this on-demand path

domain.description: The domain, exactly as configured in `AcmeOptions.Domains`.

hasCertificate.description:
true once this domain has had at least one certificate successfully
                issued -- false means no certificate has ever been issued for it at
                all, a real, distinct state from "issued, but not due for renewal yet."

issuedAtUtc.description: When the current certificate was issued, or null if Ninlil.Web.Models.AcmeCertificateInventoryEntry.HasCertificate is false.

expiresAtUtc.description: When the current certificate expires, or null if Ninlil.Web.Models.AcmeCertificateInventoryEntry.HasCertificate is false.

isDueForRenewal.description:
true when this domain has no certificate yet, or its current one is
                inside `AcmeOptions.RenewBeforeExpiration` of its own expiry -- the exact same
                condition `AcmeCertificateRenewalService`'s own poll loop uses to decide whether to
                actually attempt an issuance/renewal on its next tick, computed by the same shared method
                so this can never drift from what the background loop itself will do.

lastFailureAtUtc.description:
When this domain's own most recent issuance/renewal attempt failed, or
null if its most recent attempt succeeded (or it has never been
attempted at all).

lastFailureMessage.description:
A short, human-readable description of why the most recent attempt failed, or
null alongside Ninlil.Web.Models.AcmeCertificateInventoryEntry.LastFailureAtUtc.

AcmeCertificateInventoryEntry.description:
This record is one row of the real, per-domain certificate inventory
`AcmeSettingsController.Certificates` returns -- every domain
`AcmeOptions.Domains` currently names, alongside whatever `IAcmeAccountStore`
actually knows about it. A domain that has never had a certificate successfully issued is
always visibly distinguishable from one that simply is not due for renewal yet:
Ninlil.Web.Models.AcmeCertificateInventoryEntry.HasCertificate is false for the former and
true for the latter, regardless of what Ninlil.Web.Models.AcmeCertificateInventoryEntry.IsDueForRenewal
itself reports for either one.

AcmeSettingsDetail.description:
This record is the REST representation of this host's own currently-effective
`AcmeOptions` plus the global-default `CaaAutoManagementOptions` (nested under
Ninlil.Web.Models.AcmeSettingsDetail.CaaAutoManagement, mirroring how the per-zone override already lives
alongside a zone's own other fields on `ZonesController`). No secret material is
involved -- the account's own private key is never exposed anywhere in this REST API, the
same "never expose this over REST, at any point" posture `DnssecKeysController`
already applies to a DNSSEC private key -- so this record's own fields are the exact same
ones a `PATCH` to the same endpoint accepts.

ActiveMqBrokerSettingsDetail.description:
This record carries `ActiveMqEventBrokerOptions`'s own settings, minus
`Password` -- see Ninlil.Web.Models.RabbitMqBrokerSettingsDetail's own doc comment.

enable.description: Whether this limiter is wired into the request pipeline at all.

AdminPasswordResetMode.description:
This enumeration describes the two ways an administrator-driven password reset (see
M:Ninlil.Web.Controllers.UsersController.ResetPassword(System.Guid,Ninlil.Web.Models.AdminResetPasswordRequest,System.Threading.CancellationToken)) can deliver the new credential to
a locked-out account. Confirmed via `AskUserQuestion` that both modes are needed, not
just one: Ninlil.Web.Models.AdminPasswordResetMode.AutoGenerate works with no SMTP server configured at all, fitting
this project's homelab-first deployment default, while Ninlil.Web.Models.AdminPasswordResetMode.EmailLink lets the
account holder pick their own new password without an administrator ever seeing it, at the
cost of requiring a working, already-configured SMTP server (see
`EmailSenderOptions`/`SmtpSettingsController`).

AdminResetPasswordRequest.description:
This class carries which delivery mode an administrator-driven password reset (see
M:Ninlil.Web.Controllers.UsersController.ResetPassword(System.Guid,Ninlil.Web.Models.AdminResetPasswordRequest,System.Threading.CancellationToken)) should use -- see
Ninlil.Web.Models.AdminPasswordResetMode's own doc comment for what each mode does.

generatedPassword.description:
The newly-generated password, shown exactly this once -- set only when
Mode is Ninlil.Web.Models.AdminPasswordResetMode.AutoGenerate;
null for Ninlil.Web.Models.AdminPasswordResetMode.EmailLink, since that mode
never learns the account holder's new password at all.

AdminResetPasswordResult.description: This class carries the outcome of an administrator-driven password reset.

anywhere -- losing it means losing the ability to ever decrypt this specific archive

Data Protection key ring, and TLS certificate actually take effect -- this project's own

M:Ninlil.Web.Controllers.BackupController.Create(Ninlil.Web.Models.BackupCreateRequest,System.Threading.CancellationToken)'s own successful response, by contrast,
streams the encrypted archive itself as the response body -- never this or any other JSON

CloudProviderCredentialWriteRequest.description:
This class carries the fields used to fully replace an existing cloud DNS provider
credential set (`PUT /api/cloud-provider-credentials/{id}`). Unlike a TSIG key's own
shared secret (see Ninlil.Web.Models.TsigKeyWriteRequest), a cloud provider credential's own
secret material genuinely is something an operator supplied and may need to rotate --
Cloudflare/Route 53/DigitalOcean all expect a real operator to periodically rotate an API
token or access key themselves, entirely outside this project's own control. A `PUT`
therefore replaces Ninlil.Web.Models.CloudProviderCredentialWriteRequest.Credentials too, alongside every other field, matching
ordinary full-replacement semantics -- there is no reveal-again concern here the way there
would be for a server-generated secret, since the caller already knows the plaintext value
they are supplying in this very request. To change only metadata (name, comments,
disabled) without touching the stored credentials, use `PATCH` instead and omit

This record is the REST representation of
`Ninlil.Dhcp.Protocol.Dhcpv4.Dhcpv4ProtocolOptions` -- the DHCPv4 UDP transport's own
bind/port settings.

interfaceName.description: The OS-reported network interface name this override applies to (for example `eth0`), matched case-insensitively.

exclude.description: When true, this interface is excluded from Router Advertisement entirely; every field below is then ignored.

managedAddressConfiguration.description: Overrides Ninlil.Web.Models.DhcpRaSettingsDetail.ManagedAddressConfiguration for this interface, or inherits it when null.

otherConfiguration.description: Overrides Ninlil.Web.Models.DhcpRaSettingsDetail.OtherConfiguration for this interface, or inherits it when null.

routerLifetime.description: Overrides Ninlil.Web.Models.DhcpRaSettingsDetail.RouterLifetime for this interface, or inherits it when null.

currentHopLimit.description: Overrides Ninlil.Web.Models.DhcpRaSettingsDetail.CurrentHopLimit for this interface, or inherits it when null.

reachableTime.description: Overrides Ninlil.Web.Models.DhcpRaSettingsDetail.ReachableTime for this interface, or inherits it when null.

retransTimer.description: Overrides Ninlil.Web.Models.DhcpRaSettingsDetail.RetransTimer for this interface, or inherits it when null.

linkMtu.description: Overrides Ninlil.Web.Models.DhcpRaSettingsDetail.LinkMtu for this interface, or inherits it when null.

recursiveDnsServers.description: Wholesale-replaces Ninlil.Web.Models.DhcpRaSettingsDetail.RecursiveDnsServers for this interface when non-null, or inherits the global list when null.

recursiveDnsServerLifetime.description: Overrides Ninlil.Web.Models.DhcpRaSettingsDetail.RecursiveDnsServerLifetime for this interface, or inherits it when null.

dnsSearchListDomains.description: Wholesale-replaces Ninlil.Web.Models.DhcpRaSettingsDetail.DnsSearchListDomains for this interface when non-null, or inherits the global list when null.

dnsSearchListLifetime.description: Overrides Ninlil.Web.Models.DhcpRaSettingsDetail.DnsSearchListLifetime for this interface, or inherits it when null.

DhcpRaInterfaceOverrideDetail.description: This record is the REST representation of one `Ninlil.Dhcp.Server.Ra.RaInterfaceOverrideOptions` entry -- one network interface's own distinct Router Advertisement content, nested inside Ninlil.Web.Models.DhcpRaSettingsDetail/the `PATCH ra` merge-patch body's own `interfaceOverrides` array. Every scalar field below is nullable and, left null, inherits Ninlil.Web.Models.DhcpRaSettingsDetail's own matching global field verbatim for this one interface -- the same shape `Ninlil.Dhcp.Server.Ra.RaInterfaceOverrideOptions`'s own doc comment describes in full, including Ninlil.Web.Models.DhcpRaInterfaceOverrideDetail.RecursiveDnsServers/Ninlil.Web.Models.DhcpRaInterfaceOverrideDetail.DnsSearchListDomains's own "null inherits the global list, non-null (even empty) wholesale-replaces it" list-level rule. Deliberately excludes an override's own would-be `Prefixes`/`Routes` lists, exactly mirroring Ninlil.Web.Models.DhcpRaSettingsDetail's own established "`Prefixes` stays config-file-only" scope boundary -- extended here to `Routes` as well, since nesting a repeatable route list inside this already- repeatable interface-override list is a materially bigger REST/UI lift than everything else this record carries. Both remain fully configurable directly in the JSON configuration file (`RaInterfaceOverrideOptions.Prefixes`/`.Routes`), a genuine, deliberate scope cut rather than an oversight.

enable.description: Whether this listener binds its raw ICMPv6 socket and sends/answers Router Advertisement traffic at all.

minRouterAdvertisementInterval.description: The shortest interval between two unsolicited advertisements on the same interface.

maxRouterAdvertisementInterval.description: The longest interval between two unsolicited advertisements on the same interface.

DhcpRaProtocolSettingsDetail.description:
This record is the REST representation of
`Ninlil.Dhcp.Protocol.Ra.RaProtocolOptions` -- how this server's own Router
Advertisement listener binds and times its unsolicited advertisements. What a Router
Advertisement actually contains is Ninlil.Web.Models.DhcpRaSettingsDetail's own concern
instead, mirroring that same split in the underlying `Options` classes.

prefix.description: The route's own prefix, or null/empty when PrefixLength is `0` (a default-route-preference-only entry).

prefixLength.description: The number of leading significant bits of Prefix, `0` through `128`.

routeLifetime.description: How long this route remains valid, from the moment each advertisement carrying it is sent.

DhcpRaRouteDetail.description:
This record is the REST representation of one `Ninlil.Dhcp.Server.Ra.RaAdvertisedRouteOptions`
entry -- one specific route advertised via RFC 4191 Section 2.3's own Route Information
option, nested inside Ninlil.Web.Models.DhcpRaSettingsDetail/the `PATCH ra` merge-patch
body's own `routes` array.

managedAddressConfiguration.description: RFC 4861's own "M" flag -- hosts should obtain addresses via DHCPv6 stateful assignment.

otherConfiguration.description: RFC 4861's own "O" flag -- hosts should still use DHCPv6 for configuration other than the address itself.

routerLifetime.description: How long a host may consider this server usable as its own default router; zero means never.

currentHopLimit.description: The hop limit value recommended for outgoing unicast packets; zero means no recommendation.

reachableTime.description: How long an address is assumed reachable absent contrary evidence; zero means no recommendation.

retransTimer.description: How long a host should wait before retransmitting a Neighbor Solicitation; zero means no recommendation.

linkMtu.description: The link's own MTU, or null to advertise no MTU option at all.

recursiveDnsServers.description: The Recursive DNS Server (RFC 8106 Section 5.1) addresses advertised to a SLAAC-configured host.

recursiveDnsServerLifetime.description: How long a host should trust RecursiveDnsServers.

dnsSearchListDomains.description: The DNS Search List (RFC 8106 Section 5.2) domain suffixes advertised to a SLAAC-configured host.

dnsSearchListLifetime.description: How long a host should trust DnsSearchListDomains.

routes.description: Every specific route advertised via RFC 4191 Section 2.3's own Route Information option.

interfaceOverrides.description:
Every network interface's own explicit content override -- see
Ninlil.Web.Models.DhcpRaInterfaceOverrideDetail's own doc comment for the exact "nullable field
inherits the fields above" shape and for why, unlike Ninlil.Web.Models.DhcpRaSettingsDetail.Routes, an override's
own would-be nested prefix/route lists have no REST/UI surface here.

DhcpRaSettingsDetail.description: This record is the REST representation of the scalar/list fields of `Ninlil.Dhcp.Server.Ra.RaOptions` -- what a Router Advertisement this server sends actually contains, the content counterpart to Ninlil.Web.Models.DhcpRaProtocolSettingsDetail's own transport/timing settings. Deliberately excludes `RaOptions.Prefixes`: each prefix carries several independently-flagged/lifetimed fields (on-link/autonomous flags, two separate lifetimes) that together give it a shape closer to a genuinely independent, addressable resource -- configuring advertised prefixes remains config-file-only for now, a genuine, deliberate scope boundary rather than an oversight, left for a future dedicated sub-resource (the same shape `DhcpReservationsController` already gives a scope's own reservations). Ninlil.Web.Models.DhcpRaSettingsDetail.Routes is deliberately handled differently, and does get real REST/UI coverage here: an RFC 4191 route is a simpler, self-contained triple (prefix/prefix length, preference, lifetime) with no independent flags of its own, so it fits this controller's existing whole-array-replace shape -- the same one Ninlil.Web.Models.DhcpRaSettingsDetail.RecursiveDnsServers/Ninlil.Web.Models.DhcpRaSettingsDetail.DnsSearchListDomains already use -- rather than needing a genuinely separate, identity-bearing sub-resource the way a database-backed entity (a DHCP reservation, a scope's own custom option) does. `RaOptions` itself has no database backing at all -- every field here, this one included, lives in the JSON configuration file and is restart-required -- so a sub-resource pattern built around a persisted entity's own stable identifier does not actually fit the way this data is stored; a `PUT`-style whole-list replace on save does.

enable.description: Whether this server acts as a DHCPv4 relay agent at all.

upstreamServerAddresses.description: The IPv4 addresses of every upstream DHCPv4 server this relay forwards to.

upstreamServerPort.description: The UDP port every configured upstream DHCPv4 server listens on.

relayAgentAddress.description:
The IPv4 address this relay identifies itself as via `giaddr`, or
null for auto-detection at startup.

relayAgentCircuitId.description: The Agent Circuit ID text this relay adds to every forwarded request, if any.

relayAgentRemoteId.description: The Agent Remote ID text this relay adds to every forwarded request, if any.

This record is the REST representation of `Ninlil.Dhcp.Server.Relay.Dhcpv4RelayOptions`

itself from local scope/lease state.

scopeName.description: The name of the scope these figures describe.

The total number of slots the scope's own configured range holds, as a decimal string -- an
ordinary address for an Ninlil.Dhcp.Data.Abstractions.Enum.DhcpScopeKindEnum.AddressAssignment scope, or a
block-aligned delegable prefix for a Ninlil.Dhcp.Data.Abstractions.Enum.DhcpScopeKindEnum.PrefixDelegation one.

offeredCount.description: The number of slots currently tentatively offered, awaiting confirmation.

DhcpScopeStatisticsDetail.description:
This record is the REST representation of `Ninlil.Dhcp.Server.Core.Statistics.DhcpScopeStatistics`
-- a single DHCP scope's own genuine, freshly-computed utilization, never a cached or
approximate figure (see that class's own doc comment for exactly how each field is

string, not a JSON number: an IPv6 `AddressAssignment` scope's own configured range can
legitimately hold far more addresses than fit in a JSON number's own safe-integer range (an
ordinary `/64` alone holds 2^64 of them) without losing precision.

name.description: An operator-chosen, human-readable, unique name for this scope.

rangeStartAddress.description: The first address in the pool this scope hands leases out from, inclusive.

rangeEndAddress.description: The last address in the pool this scope hands leases out from, inclusive.

subnetPrefixLength.description: The CIDR prefix length, in bits, of the network the range belongs to.

defaultLeaseDuration.description: The lease duration granted to a client that does not request a specific one.

maxLeaseDuration.description: The longest lease duration this scope ever grants.

isDisabled.description: Whether the scope starts out (or is currently) disabled.

gatewayAddresses.description: The router (default gateway) addresses this scope hands out, in order of preference.

dnsServerAddresses.description: The DNS server addresses this scope hands out, in order of preference.

comments.description: Free-form operator notes about this scope.

The identifier of the DNS zone a lease drawn from this scope should auto-register an
A/AAAA record for its own presented host name into, or null to leave
DHCP->DNS integration disabled for this scope.

The name of the boot file a PXE client drawing a lease from this scope should request, or
null to offer no boot file at all -- see
`DhcpScopeEntity.BootFileName`'s own doc comment.

nextServerAddress.description:
The address of the TFTP (or other boot) server a PXE client should contact for
BootFileName, or null to fall back to this server's
own Server Identifier address -- see `DhcpScopeEntity.NextServerAddress`'s own doc
comment.

delegatedPrefixLength.description:
The length, in bits, of each individual prefix this scope delegates to a client -- required
when Kind is Ninlil.Dhcp.Data.Abstractions.Enum.DhcpScopeKindEnum.PrefixDelegation, and
rejected (must be null) otherwise -- see
`DhcpScopeEntity.DelegatedPrefixLength`'s own doc comment.

DhcpServiceKindEnum.description:
This enumeration names each of the four DHCP-family services
Ninlil.Web.Controllers.DhcpServiceControlController reports on/controls -- one entry
per real `Ninlil.Dhcp.Common.Control.IDhcpProtocolService` implementation this project
registers. The `{kind}` route segment on
M:Ninlil.Web.Controllers.DhcpServiceControlController.Start(Ninlil.Web.Models.DhcpServiceKindEnum,System.Threading.CancellationToken)/
M:Ninlil.Web.Controllers.DhcpServiceControlController.Stop(Ninlil.Web.Models.DhcpServiceKindEnum,System.Threading.CancellationToken) binds directly to this
enumeration (case-insensitively, ASP.NET Core's own default model-binding behavior for an
enum route parameter), so an unrecognized route segment is rejected by model binding itself
before this controller's own action ever runs.

enabled.description:
Whether this service is configured to start automatically at the next host boot -- this
server's own `Enable` option for this protocol, read fresh on every call, never a
stale snapshot.

isRunning.description: Whether this service's own listener is genuinely bound and serving traffic right now.

DhcpServiceStatus.description:
This record is the REST representation of one DHCP-family service's own current state --
both its configured Ninlil.Web.Models.DhcpServiceStatus.Enabled flag (whether it starts automatically at host
boot) and its actual, live Ninlil.Web.Models.DhcpServiceStatus.IsRunning signal, which can legitimately differ
from it in either direction: a service configured false can still be
running right now (started live, after boot, through this same controller), and a service
configured true can legitimately not be running (stopped live, or --
Ninlil.Web.Models.DhcpServiceKindEnum.Tftp only -- declined to bind at all for a real,
non-throwing precondition failure such as a missing root directory; see
`TftpServer`'s own doc comment) -- see
`Ninlil.Dhcp.Common.Control.IDhcpProtocolService`'s own doc comment for why these
two are deliberately distinct concepts throughout this whole feature.

relayInterfaceIdHex.description: The DHCPv6 Interface-ID value this rule requires, as hex, if any (DHCPv6 only).

vendorClassEnterpriseNumber.description: The IANA Enterprise Number a DHCPv6 Vendor Class option must carry, if any (DHCPv6 only).

DnsCookieSettingsDetail.description:
This record is the REST representation of this host's own currently-effective
`DnsCookieOptions` (RFC 7873). No secret material is involved, so this record's own
fields are the exact same ones a `PATCH` to the same endpoint accepts.

enable.description: Whether this transport listens at all. Genuinely live: toggling this field starts or stops the real, already-running `dnscrypt-udp`/`dnscrypt-tcp` listeners and`dnscrypt-certificate-rotation` (the background loop that actually issues this resolver's own DNSCrypt certificates -- with no certificate, a live-started listener could accept connections but never answer a real encrypted query), all three registered with Ninlil.Web.Services.IManagedServiceRegistry, with no restart.

port.description: The port this transport binds to, for both UDP and TCP. Restart-required.

providerName.description: The zone this resolver advertises its DNSCrypt certificate discovery TXT record under. Restart-required -- read once, at this transport's own startup.

tcpIdleTimeout.description: How long a TCP connection may sit completely idle before this server closes it. Restart-required.

maxConcurrentTcpConnections.description: How many TCP connections this server accepts at once. Restart-required.

enabledEsVersions.description:
Every DNSCrypt cipher this resolver keeps a continuously valid certificate for, by name (for
example `["XChaCha20Poly1305", "XSalsa20Poly1305"]`). Restart-required --
`DnsCryptCertificateRotationService` reads this once per rotation check, not per
request, so a change here needs that background loop (or the whole transport, since this
controller restarts it together with the listeners) to restart before it takes effect.

certificateRotationInterval.description: How often a fresh certificate is considered for every enabled cipher. Restart-required.

certificateValidityDuration.description: How long a newly generated certificate stays valid for. Restart-required.

certificateClockSkewTolerance.description: How far in the past a newly generated certificate's own validity start is backdated. Restart-required.

DnsCryptSettingsDetail.description: This record is the REST representation of DNSCrypt's own `DnsCryptOptions`.

enable.description: Whether a DNS-over-HTTPS request reaching the already-mapped route is answered. Genuinely live: toggling this field starts or stops the real `dns-over-https` transport gate registered with Ninlil.Web.Services.IManagedServiceRegistry, with no restart -- the route itself is always mapped, regardless of this flag's own value at process startup, so there is no "route was never mapped" edge case left to work around (see that extension method's own doc comment).

path.description: The HTTP path both the GET and POST forms of a DoH query are answered at. Needs a full process restart, not merely a listener restart -- ASP.NET Core's Minimal API routing has no supported "remap this route" operation once the host has started.

maxMessageSizeBytes.description:
How large a single DNS message this transport accepts may be. Needs a full process restart
for the same reason as Ninlil.Web.Models.DnsOverHttpsSettingsDetail.Path -- both are captured once, into the closure the
route itself was mapped with.

DnsOverHttpsSettingsDetail.description:
This record is the REST representation of DNS-over-HTTPS's own `DnsOverHttpsOptions`,
as actually consulted by this combined host: `Port` and `Certificate` are
deliberately excluded, because M:Ninlil.Dns.Protocol.DnsOverHttps.Extension.EndpointRouteBuilderDnsOverHttpsExtension.MapNinlilDnsOverHttps(Microsoft.AspNetCore.Routing.IEndpointRouteBuilder)
maps RFC 8484's GET/POST forms directly onto this host's own already-running shared Kestrel
instance -- both fields are specific to `DnsOverHttpsHostedService`'s own separate,
self-hosted Kestrel instance, which this composition root never starts, and would be
silently ignored (misleadingly, if exposed here as if they mattered) if written through this
controller. This host's own shared HTTP(S) port and certificate decide both instead.

enable.description: Whether this transport listens at all. Genuinely live: toggling this field starts or stops the real, already-running `dns-over-quic` listener registered with Ninlil.Web.Services.IManagedServiceRegistry, with no restart.

port.description: The port this transport binds to. Restart-required.

idleTimeout.description: How long a QUIC connection may sit completely idle before this server closes it. Restart-required.

maxConcurrentBidirectionalStreams.description: How many bidirectional streams a single QUIC connection may have open at once. Restart-required.

DnsOverQuicSettingsDetail.description: This record is the REST representation of DNS-over-QUIC's own `DnsOverQuicOptions`.

enable.description: Whether a connection from a recognized source is inspected for a PROXY protocol header at all.

knownProxies.description: Every individual IP address allowed to open a connection carrying a PROXY protocol header.

knownNetworks.description: Every CIDR network allowed to open a connection carrying a PROXY protocol header.

DnsOverTlsProxyProtocolSettingsDetail.description:
This record is the REST representation of `Ninlil.Dns.Protocol.DnsOverTls.ProxyProtocol.ProxyProtocolOptions`
-- whether `DnsOverTlsListener` accepts a HAProxy-style PROXY protocol header (v1
text or v2 binary) ahead of its own TLS handshake, and which addresses/networks are
trusted to send one. Unlike the HTTP-side allowlist above, there is no shared-secret field
here at all -- see `ProxyProtocolOptions`'s own doc comment for why.

enable.description: Whether this transport listens at all. Genuinely live: toggling this field, via M:Ninlil.Web.Controllers.TransportSettingsController.PatchDnsOverTls(System.Text.Json.JsonElement,System.Threading.CancellationToken), starts or stops the real, already-running `dns-over-tls` listener registered with Ninlil.Web.Services.IManagedServiceRegistry, with no restart.

port.description: The port this transport binds to. Restart-required -- rebinding a socket to a new port needs this specific listener to restart.

idleTimeout.description: How long a TLS connection may sit completely idle before this server closes it. Restart-required -- read once when a connection is accepted, under this listener's own currently-bound socket.

maxConcurrentConnections.description: How many TLS connections this server accepts at once. Restart-required, for the same reason as Ninlil.Web.Models.DnsOverTlsSettingsDetail.IdleTimeout.

DnsOverTlsSettingsDetail.description:
This record is the REST representation of DNS-over-TLS's own `DnsOverTlsOptions`.
Deliberately excludes `ProxyProtocol` -- already exposed via
Ninlil.Web.Controllers.ReverseProxySettingsController's own `dnsOverTls` nested
field, alongside the HTTP-side reverse-proxy trust settings it is conceptually paired with;
duplicating it here would give the same configuration section two different REST addresses.

DnsPipelineSettingsDetail.description:
This record is the REST representation of this host's own currently-effective
`DnsQueryProcessingPipelineOptions` -- worker-pool/queue sizing plus UDP
amplification-guard tuning. This record's own fields are the exact same ones a
`PATCH` to the same endpoint accepts.

occurredAtUtc.description: The UTC date and time the query finished being answered.

clientAddress.description: The querying client's own source address, or null if none was known.

queriedName.description: The queried name's own presentation form, or null if the query carried no question at all.

answerCount.description: How many records the answer's own Answer section carried.

clientIdentifier.description:
The querying client's own persistent identifier (a MAC address or DUID), resolved once at
write time, or null when it was never resolved or the configured query
logging privacy level suppresses it -- see
Ninlil.Dns.Server.QueryLog.DnsQueryLogSubscriber's own doc comment for the
full reasoning.

DnsQueryLogEntryDetail.description:
This class carries a single persisted query log entry's own fields, for
`QueryLogController`'s own search response. No secret material is involved anywhere
in this entity, so, unlike several other entity types in this project, there is no
reveal-once policy to apply here at all -- every field is always fully visible to any
caller holding `querylog:read`.

skip.description: How many items were skipped before this page began.

take.description: The maximum number of items this page could contain.

totalCount.description: The total number of items across every page.

domain.description: This rewrite's own domain pattern, exactly as stored.

target.description: This rewrite's own target, exactly as stored.

isDisabled.description: Whether this rewrite is currently disabled.

comments.description: Free-form operator notes about this rewrite.

updatedAtUtc.description: When this rewrite was last modified, or null if never.

originatingNodeId.description:
The cluster node this rewrite was last created or modified on (the cluster's own
operational config sync), or null on a deployment that has never had clustering
enabled.

clientId.description:
The single known client (`Ninlil.Dns.Data.Abstractions.Entity.DnsClientEntity`) this
rewrite is scoped to, or null if it is unscoped (global) or scoped to a
client group instead -- read-only here: the ordinary create/replace/patch actions on this
controller never set it, since the only real write path that ever scopes a rewrite is
`SafeSearchController.Enable`'s own optional target. Surfaced so an operator browsing
the ordinary Rewrites page can tell a Safe-Search-scoped row apart from a global one, rather
than seeing what would otherwise look like an unexplained, untargetable duplicate.

clientGroupId.description:
The single client group this rewrite is scoped to, or null if it is
unscoped or scoped to one specific client instead -- the same read-only, informational
purpose Ninlil.Web.Models.DnsRewriteDetail.ClientId serves.

DnsRewriteDetail.description:
This class carries a single DNS rewrite's own fields, for list, single-item, and creation
responses. No secret material is involved anywhere in this entity, so, unlike
`TsigKeyDetail`/`DnssecKeyDetail`/`CloudProviderCredentialDetail`/
`WebhookSubscriptionDetail`, there is no reveal-once policy to apply here at all.

skip.description: How many items were skipped before this page began.

take.description: The maximum number of items this page could contain.

totalCount.description: The total number of items across every page.

DnsRewriteDetailPagedResult.description:
This class wraps a single page of a larger list -- the shape every list endpoint in this
project's REST API returns, offset/limit paginated (a sane default/max page size is enough
at this project's own homelab/small-org target scale; a cursor-based scheme's extra
complexity is not needed).

domain.description:
The queried domain this rewrite matches -- an exact name with no `*` character, or a
shell-style wildcard glob (`*.example.com`) with one. Validated as a syntactically
valid domain name before this rewrite is ever persisted.

target.description:
Either a literal IP address (an A/AAAA-style rewrite) or another domain name (a
CNAME-style rewrite) -- validated against the real
`DnsRewriteTargetClassifier.TryClassify` before this rewrite is ever persisted, the
same "validate against the real codec/parser" discipline Ninlil.Web.Controllers.RecordsController
already applies to a record's own `data` field.

isDisabled.description: Whether the rewrite starts out (or is currently) disabled.

comments.description: Free-form operator notes about this rewrite.

This class carries the fields used to create or fully replace a DNS rewrite
(`POST`/`PUT /api/dns-rewrites`).

keySizeBits.description:
The key size to generate, in bits -- meaningful only for the RSA algorithm family; ignored
for every other algorithm.

comments.description: Free-form operator notes about the key.

DnssecKeyCreateRequest.description:
This class carries the fields used to generate a new DNSSEC key for a zone
(`POST /api/zones/{zoneId}/dnssec-keys`). Ninlil only ever generates a brand-new
keypair server-side -- there is no way to import an externally-generated private key.

zoneId.description: The identifier of the zone this key belongs to.

publicKeyWireFormat.description: The key's public key material, base64-encoded.

keyTag.description: The key's precomputed key tag (RFC 4034 Appendix B).

isRetired.description:
Whether the key has been fully withdrawn from the zone's own DNSKEY RRset -- equivalent to
`LifecycleState == Removed`, kept as its own field for the REST/UI contract that
predates Ninlil.Web.Models.DnssecKeyDetail.LifecycleState.

comments.description: Free-form operator notes about the key.

updatedAtUtc.description: When the key's own metadata was last updated, if ever.

publishedAtUtc.description: When the key was first published in the zone's own DNSKEY RRset.

retiredAtUtc.description:
When the key most recently stopped being its zone's own canonical, currently-signing key
of its role, or null if it never has.

parentDsConfirmedAtUtc.description:
When an operator confirmed a KSK rollover's own new DS record has actually been published
at a real, externally-hosted parent zone, or null if no such
confirmation has been recorded (either because no rollover needs one, or because it is
still awaited).

dnsKeyRecord.description: The key's DNSKEY record in presentation format, as published in the zone.

dsRecord.description:
The SHA-256 DS record a parent zone publishes for this key, in presentation format, or
null for a ZSK, which the parent never references.

dsDigest.description:
The digest part of DsRecord on its own, as uppercase hexadecimal, for
registrars that ask for the key tag, algorithm, digest type and digest separately.

DnssecKeyDetail.description:
This class carries a DNSSEC key's own metadata, for list and single-item responses. This
deliberately never includes the key's own private key material -- unlike a TSIG shared
secret or a cloud provider credential, a DNSSEC private key never needs to leave this
server; it exists purely for `Server.Authoritative`'s own internal signing, so it
stays encrypted at rest and is never exposed over this REST API at all, at any point in a
key's lifecycle.

skip.description: How many items were skipped before this page began.

take.description: The maximum number of items this page could contain.

totalCount.description: The total number of items across every page.

This class wraps a single page of a larger list -- the shape every list endpoint in this

complexity is not needed).

keySizeBits.description: The new key's own key size, in bits -- meaningful only for the RSA algorithm family.

DnssecKeyRolloverRequest.description:
This class carries the fields used to start an automated RFC 6781 key rollover for an
existing, currently-active key (`POST /api/zones/{zoneId}/dnssec-keys/{id}/roll`).
Ninlil chooses the rollover scheme by the existing key's own `Role` -- Pre-Publish
(RFC 6781 §4.1.1.1) for a ZSK, Double-Signature (RFC 6781 §4.1.2) for a KSK -- there is no
way to request the other scheme for a given role through this action.

DnssecKeyRolloverSettingsDetail.description:
This record is the REST representation of this host's own currently-effective
`DnssecKeyRolloverOptions` -- the RFC 6781 §4.1.1.1/§4.1.2 key-rollover timing
`DnssecKeyRolloverBackgroundService` walks every locally signed zone's own keys
against. No secret material is involved, so this record's own fields are the exact same
ones a `PATCH` to the same endpoint accepts.

isRetired.description: Whether the key is retired (taken out of active signing use).

comments.description: Free-form operator notes about the key.

DnssecKeyWriteRequest.description:
This class carries the fields used to fully replace an existing DNSSEC key's own mutable
state (`PUT /api/zones/{zoneId}/dnssec-keys/{id}`). A key's role, algorithm, and key
material are permanent once generated -- rolling to a different algorithm or role means
generating a brand-new key and retiring the old one, not editing this one in place -- so
retirement status and operator notes are the only fields this resource ever exposes as
writable.

allowedAlgorithms.description:
The only algorithms a new key may use. An empty list (the default) means no restriction at
all -- every algorithm this server's own `DnssecAlgorithmRegistry` supports may be
used. This restricts only the *generation* of new signing keys, never the validation of an
already-signed, externally-hosted zone's own algorithm choice -- a known, deliberate scope
cut.

DnssecPolicySettingsDetail.description:
This record is the REST representation of this host's own currently-effective
`DnssecAlgorithmPolicyOptions` -- which DNSSEC algorithms
`IDnssecKeyManagementService.GenerateKeyAsync` is willing to generate a brand-new
signing key for. No secret material is involved, so this record's own field is the exact
same one a `PATCH` to the same endpoint accepts.

isConnected.description:
Whether the active broker transport currently reports itself connected --
null when Ninlil.Web.Models.EventBrokerSettingsDetail.Transport is
Ninlil.Dns.Common.Enum.EventTransportEnum.InMemory, since "connected" has no meaning there.

lastModifiedUtc.description:
When this settings section was last written (the cluster's own operational config sync), or
null if it has never been written through this REST surface.

originatingNodeId.description:
The cluster node this settings section was last written on, or null
alongside Ninlil.Web.Models.EventBrokerSettingsDetail.LastModifiedUtc.

EventBrokerSettingsDetail.description:
This record is the REST representation of this host's own currently-effective message-
broker event-transport configuration. Only the section matching Ninlil.Web.Models.EventBrokerSettingsDetail.Transport is
ever populated -- the other is null, since a value read from
Microsoft.Extensions.Options.IOptions`1 for a broker that was never
selected (and therefore never had its own `Configure<TOptions>` called) would
otherwise just be that options class's own compiled-in defaults, which would misleadingly
look like real, live configuration.

This class carries a block/allow list's own metadata, for list, single-item, and
